To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermophoretics and photophoreses of aerosol cylinders are different from those of spherical particles because of the different specific surface areas and the effects of thermal stress slip.
the photophoretics of aerosol cylinders and spheres have similar characteristics, and the thermophoresis of the former can be smaller than that of the latter.

the thermophoreticity and photophoreticity of aerosol particles are affected by thermal creep, temperature-jump, frictional slip and thermal stress slip, and the effects of thermal creep and thermal stress slip can be significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of thermal creep, temperature-jump, and frictional slip on the thermophoresis of aerosol particles and with the effect of these factors and thermal-stress slip on the photophoresis.
the effects of thermal creep, temperature-jump, and thermal stress-slip boundary conditions at the particle surface on the photophoretically driven motion of an aerosol particle.
the thermophoresis of aerosol particles with slip-flow boundary conditions, and the effects of particle size and thermal stress slip on the photophoresis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thermal stress slip has a significant impact on the thermophoresis of aerosol particles and a negligible impact on the photophoresis.
the photophoretically induced velocity is more sensitive to the optical properties of the particles than the thermophoretically induced one.

the effect of thermal creep is always significant for the case where the thermal conductivity of a gaseous medium is much smaller than that of the aerosol, but is negligible when the thermal conductivity of an aerosol is smaller than that the gaseous phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a given particle, the thermal creep effect on its mobility is more significant than the thermal stress slip effect, but for a given ambient fluid, the thermal stress slip can be a dominant factor for its mobility.
the photophoretically induced particle motion is much more sensitive to the optical properties of a particle than is the thermophoresis.

, for the case of moderately small Knudden number, the thermal stress slip at a particle surface has a significant effect on the thermophoresis of the particle, and the effect on its photophoretis is also important for not too small optical thickness.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the photophoretically driven motion of an aerosol particle is more complicated than its thermophoretic motion and the effects of the thermal stress slip at particle surface on the photophoretism of an aerosol are more significant than those on thermophoresis.
the photophoretically driven aerosol cylinder is more efficient for particle collection in comparison to the spherical particle.

the photophoretically induced motion of a cylindrical particle may be more significant in the presence of thermal stress slip than that of a spherically shaped particle, especially when the Knudsen number is not too small and the particle has a relatively high thermal conductivity and a small specific surface area.
